a: a drifting hired hand
t: A homeless hired hand, or one hired for a year?
p: Vaticanus has a hired man "without a hearth"; other copies and the Hebrew have one hired "for a year."

readings.w: Greek: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD) as printed by Swete
readings.en: a hireling away from his hearth
readings.plain: a drifting hired hand

readings.w: Greek: a corrector of Codex Sinaiticus (ℵ) and Codex Alexandrinus (A, 400s AD), in forms of ἐπετείου, "yearly," as Swete's notes give them; the KJV ("an hireling for a year"); Hebrew manuscript D of the Cairo Genizah, שכיר שנה
readings.en: a hireling for a year
readings.plain: a hired hand taken on for a year

why: The Plain English Translation follows the base text. The other reading, a worker hired by the year, is well supported and agrees with the Hebrew, so it may be what the grandson wrote. In either case the point is that a hired man has no stake in finishing the job.

a: will inherit trust
p: The Greek has "trust" (pistis); the Hebrew of manuscript D has "honor."

readings.w: Greek: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD) as printed by Swete
readings.en: will inherit trust
readings.plain: will inherit trust

readings.w: Hebrew manuscript D of the Cairo Genizah, ינהל כבוד; the KJV has "glory"
readings.en: will inherit honor
readings.plain: will inherit honor

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Greek. The Hebrew "honor" (kavod) fits the parallel line about a lasting name. Manuscript D goes on, "and his name stands in eternal life," an idiom here for a name that lasts forever. The Plain English Translation keeps "inherit" for the Greek klēronomeō, as everywhere in Sirach.

a: brings pain
p: Vaticanus has "pain"; Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and both Hebrew copies have "sickness."

readings.w: Greek: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD) as printed by Swete
readings.en: there will be pain
readings.plain: brings pain

readings.w: Greek: Codex Sinaiticus (ℵ) and Codex Alexandrinus (A), νόσος, as Swete's notes give them; the Latin Vulgate (its 37:33), "infirmitas"; the KJV ("sickness"); Hebrew: manuscript B (folio VIII recto, line 4) and manuscript D (folio II verso, lines 18-19) of the Cairo Genizah, חולי
readings.en: there will be sickness
readings.plain: brings sickness

why: The Plain English Translation follows the base text. "Sickness" has wide support, in two codices, the Latin and both Hebrew copies, and it fits the doctor passage that follows; the two Greek words differ by two letters.

a: as though you were no more
t: "As though you were no more," or "as your means allow"?
p: The Greek is obscure; the Hebrew of manuscript B says to make the offering as rich as your wealth allows.

readings.w: Greek: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD) as printed by Swete and the other Greek copies
readings.en: as one not existing
readings.plain: as though you were no more

readings.w: Hebrew manuscript B of the Cairo Genizah (Kahana's edition), בכנפי הוניך; compare 14:11
readings.en: by the edges (limits) of your wealth
readings.plain: as far as your means allow

why: The Plain English Translation keeps the Greek, which may mean "as one who is about to die," giving generously because life is at stake. The Hebrew is clearer and fits Ben Sira's advice at 14:11, "My child, as much as you have, do yourself good, / and bring the Lord the offerings he deserves."

a: may he fall into a doctor's hands!
t: Falling into a doctor's hands, or defying the doctor?
p: The Greek wishes the sinner into a doctor's hands; the Hebrew of manuscript B says he will defy the doctor.

readings.w: Greek: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD) as printed by Swete; its margin in Hebrew manuscript B has a close form
readings.en: may he fall into a physician's hands
readings.plain: may he fall into a doctor's hands!

readings.w: Hebrew manuscript B of the Cairo Genizah, main text: יתגבר לפני רופא
readings.en: he will act proudly before a physician
readings.plain: he will act defiantly before a doctor.

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Greek, which the churches received. The margin of manuscript B reads "will be handed over into the hands of a physician," which supports the Greek. The main Hebrew text gives a different and gentler point: the sinner proves his pride by refusing help.

a: grief also should pass by
p: Vaticanus says grief "passes by"; Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus say it "remains," as the KJV has.

readings.w: Greek: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD) as printed by Swete
readings.en: grief also passes by
readings.plain: grief also should pass by

readings.w: Greek: Codex Sinaiticus (ℵ, 300s AD, as corrected) and Codex Alexandrinus (A); the KJV ("sorrow remaineth")
readings.en: grief also remains
readings.plain: grief also remains

why: The Plain English Translation follows Vaticanus, which fits the advice to let grief end (38:20-23). The other reading describes how grief lingers. Hebrew manuscript B has no line for this verse.

a: hardens his skin
p: One Greek letter separates "hardens" (Vaticanus) from "melts" (Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus).

readings.w: Greek: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD) as printed by Swete
readings.en: the vapor of fire will harden his flesh
readings.plain: hardens his skin

readings.w: Greek: Codex Sinaiticus (ℵ) and Codex Alexandrinus (A); the KJV ("wasteth his flesh")
readings.en: the vapor of fire will melt his flesh
readings.plain: melts his skin away

why: The Plain English Translation follows the base text. Both readings make sense of a smith's life by the furnace. The Hebrew of this verse is lost from manuscript B.

a: finishing the fine piece
t: The fine piece, or the glaze?
p: Vaticanus has charisma, "a thing of grace"; Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus have chrisma, "coating, glaze."

readings.w: Greek: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD) as printed by Swete (first hand and a later hand)
readings.en: to complete the gracious work
readings.plain: finishing the fine piece

readings.w: Greek: a corrector of Codex Vaticanus, Codex Sinaiticus (ℵ) and Codex Alexandrinus (A); the KJV ("to lead it over")
readings.en: to complete the coating
readings.plain: finishing the glaze

why: The Plain English Translation follows Swete's text. The glaze reading fits a potter's work well and may be original; the two words differ by one letter.

a: no one could live there as a stranger or walk about
t: A line added about the council
p: A corrector of Sinaiticus adds a line about the people's council, which the KJV also has.

readings.w: Greek: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD) as printed by Swete
readings.en: and they will not sojourn or walk about
readings.plain: no one could live there as a stranger or walk about

readings.w: Greek: a corrector of Codex Sinaiticus (ℵ c.a), as Swete's notes print it; the KJV has "They shall not be sought for in publick counsel"
readings.orig: καὶ οὐ παροικήσουσιν οὐδὲ περιπατήσουσιν, ἀλλ᾽ εἰς βουλὴν λαοῦ ζητηθήσονται
readings.en: and they will not sojourn or walk about, but they will be sought for the people's council
readings.plain: no one could live there as a stranger or walk about, / but they will be sought out for the people's council

why: The Plain English Translation follows Vaticanus, which lacks the line. Swete's note gives the added words without "not," so in Sinaiticus's corrected text the workers are sought for the council, and 38:33 then says the opposite. The KJV's line, at its 38:33, has the "not": "They shall not be sought for in publick counsel."

a: make righteousness and justice plain
p: Vaticanus has "righteousness and justice"; Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus have "instruction and justice."

readings.w: Greek: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD) as printed by Swete
readings.en: make righteousness and judgment plain
readings.plain: make righteousness and justice plain

readings.w: Greek: Codex Sinaiticus (ℵ) and Codex Alexandrinus (A), παιδείαν (written παιδιαν), as Swete's notes give them; no Hebrew survives for this verse
readings.en: make instruction and judgment plain
readings.plain: make instruction and justice plain

why: The Plain English Translation follows the base text. Either way the line says that workers do not teach or give rulings; the other codices make the teaching explicit.

a: fine flour, wheat
t: Fine flour and wheat, or fine wheat flour?
p: Vaticanus lists "fine flour, wheat" as two things; Sinaiticus has "fine flour of wheat," one thing.

readings.w: Greek: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD) as printed by Swete
readings.en: fine flour, wheat
readings.plain: fine flour, wheat

readings.w: Greek: Codex Sinaiticus (ℵ), πυροῦ, as Swete's notes give it (Codex Ephraemi has πῦρ, "fire"); the KJV ("flour of wheat"); compare the Latin Vulgate (its 39:31), "panis similagineus," "bread of fine flour"
readings.en: fine flour of wheat
readings.plain: fine wheat flour

why: The Plain English Translation follows the base text, which lists eleven things. With Sinaiticus the list has ten. The Hebrew of manuscript B is damaged at this point.

a: in their fury they lay on their whips harder
p: The Greek has the winds harden their whips; Kahana's Hebrew has them move mountains in their anger.

readings.w: Greek: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD) as printed by Swete
readings.orig: ἐν θυμῷ αὐτῶν ἐστερέωσαν μάστιγας αὐτῶν
readings.en: in their fury they made their scourges firm
readings.plain: in their fury they lay on their whips harder

readings.w: Hebrew: Kahana's edition of manuscript B of the Cairo Genizah, ובאפם הרים יעתיקו. The leaf itself (folio IX recto, line 17, in Abegg's transcription) keeps only ם יעתיק, with the last letter restored. The Masada scroll (first century BC), column I, line 3, keeps the letters ים יע, then a gap, then יקו with a doubtful ת before it: scraps that fit the same verb
readings.en: and in their anger they move mountains
readings.plain: in their anger they move mountains

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Greek. The Hebrew pictures the storm winds tearing at the mountains. Only the verb, "they move," survives on manuscript B, and the Masada letters fit it, so the rest of the Hebrew line rests on Kahana's edition.

a: And now we have sung with all our heart and mouth
p: Vaticanus's first hand has "we have sung"; its corrector, the other codices and the Hebrew have a command to sing.

readings.w: Greek: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD) as printed by Swete (first hand)
readings.en: we sang hymns
readings.plain: And now we have sung with all our heart and mouth

readings.w: Greek: a corrector of Codex Vaticanus, Codex Sinaiticus (ℵ), Codex Alexandrinus (A) and Codex Ephraemi (C, 400s AD); Hebrew manuscript B of the Cairo Genizah, הרנינו
readings.en: sing hymns
readings.plain: And now sing with all your heart and mouth

why: The Plain English Translation follows Swete's text, which ends the hymn by looking back on it. Most witnesses, and the Hebrew "shout for joy," have a command, which matches the call to sing in 39:14-15. It may well be the original.

a: they are buried in the mother of all
t: Buried in the earth, or returning to it?
p: Vaticanus has "burial"; a corrector of Sinaiticus and the Hebrew have "return."

readings.w: Greek: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD) as printed by Swete
readings.orig: ἕως ἡμέρας ἐπὶ ταφῇ εἰς μητέρα πάντων
readings.en: until the day for burial into the mother of all
readings.plain: they are buried in the mother of all

readings.w: Greek: a corrector of Codex Sinaiticus (ℵ c.a), ἐπιστραφῇ; Hebrew manuscript B of the Cairo Genizah, עד יום שובו אל אם כל חי
readings.orig: ἕως ἡμέρας ἐπιστραφῇ εἰς μητέρα πάντων
readings.en: until the day of returning to the mother of all
readings.plain: they return to the mother of all

why: The Plain English Translation follows the base text. The Hebrew "return to the mother of all living" uses the name of Eve (Genesis 3:20) for the earth, and the Sinaiticus corrector's "return" agrees with it.

a: death and bloodshed, strife and the sword.
p: Most Greek copies add four more evils to the list, as the KJV has.

readings.w: Greek: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD) as printed by Swete (first hand)
readings.orig: θάνατος καὶ αἷμα καὶ ἔρις καὶ ῥομφαία
readings.en: death and blood and strife and sword
readings.plain: death and bloodshed, strife and the sword.

readings.w: Greek: a corrector of Codex Vaticanus (in the margin), Codex Sinaiticus (ℵ), Codex Alexandrinus (A) and Codex Ephraemi (C); the KJV
readings.orig: θάνατος καὶ αἷμα καὶ ἔρις καὶ ῥομφαία, ἐπαγωγαὶ λιμὸς καὶ σύντριμμα καὶ μάστιξ
readings.en: death and blood and strife and sword, calamities, famine, ruin and scourge
readings.plain: death and bloodshed, strife and the sword, / calamities and famine, ruin and the whip.

why: The Plain English Translation follows the first hand of Vaticanus. The longer list is in most witnesses. The Hebrew of manuscript B also has eight evils: plague and blood, fever and sword, ruin and breaking, evil and death.

a: what comes from the waters returns to the sea
t: Back to the sea, or back on high?
p: The Greek has water returning to the sea; the Hebrew has what is from on high returning on high.

readings.w: Greek: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD) as printed by Swete and the other Greek copies
readings.orig: καὶ ἀπὸ ὑδάτων εἰς θάλασσαν ἀνακάμπτει
readings.en: and from waters it turns back to the sea
readings.plain: what comes from the waters returns to the sea

readings.w: Hebrew manuscript B of the Cairo Genizah, ואשר ממרום אל מרום
readings.en: and what is from on high, to on high
readings.plain: what comes from on high returns on high

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Greek, which echoes Ecclesiastes 1:7. The Hebrew may mean the human spirit, which "goes back to God, who gave it" (Ecclesiastes 12:7), so it would hint at more than the Greek does.

a: Kindness is like a paradise rich in blessings
p: The Greek has "kindness is like a paradise"; the Masada scroll has "loyal love, like eternity, will not be cut off."

readings.w: Greek: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD) as printed by Swete
readings.en: grace is like a paradise in blessings
readings.plain: Kindness is like a paradise rich in blessings

readings.w: Hebrew: the Masada scroll (first century BC), חסד כעד לא תכרת; manuscript B of the Cairo Genizah has וחסד לעולם לא ימוט, "loyal love will never totter"
readings.en: loyal love, like eternity, will not be cut off
readings.plain: Loyal love, like eternity, will never be cut off

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Greek. The Hebrew ka'ad, "like eternity," looks like the source of the Greek "like a paradise" if the translator read ke'eden, "like Eden" (Claude's suggestion, based on 40:27, where the Hebrew does say "like an Eden").

a: the one who has enough and for the worker
t: Enough and wages, or wine and strong drink?
p: The Greek speaks of the self-sufficient and the worker; the Masada scroll of plenty and wages; manuscript B of wine and strong drink.

readings.w: Greek: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD) as printed by Swete, with no difference in Swete's notes
readings.en: the life of the self-sufficient, of the worker
readings.plain: the one who has enough and for the worker

readings.w: Hebrew: the Masada scroll (first century BC), column II, line 8, חיי יתר שכר, which Eric Reymond translates "A life of plenty <and> (a life) of wages"
readings.en: a life of plenty and of wages
readings.plain: the one who has plenty and for the wage-earner

readings.w: Hebrew: manuscript B of the Cairo Genizah (folio X recto, line 9), חיי יין ושכר, with יותר שכל, "excess and good sense," in its margin
readings.en: a life of wine and strong drink
readings.plain: the one who has wine and strong drink

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Greek. Its two words stand side by side with no "and"; the Plain English Translation takes them as two people, because "better than both" needs two, as the KJV does ("To labour, and to be content") and as Reymond's translation of the Masada line does. The Latin takes them as one, "a worker content with what he has." The Masada scroll is closest to the Greek; manuscript B has the pair "wine and strong drink," which also stands at 40:20.

a: the love of wisdom
t: Love of wisdom, or love of friends?
p: The Greek has "love of wisdom" (Ephraemi: "finding wisdom"); the Hebrew has "love of friends" (dodim).

readings.w: Greek: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD) as printed by Swete and Codex Alexandrinus (A); in Codex Sinaiticus (ℵ) the words are written over an erasure by a corrector, as Swete's notes say
readings.en: love of wisdom
readings.plain: the love of wisdom

readings.w: Greek: Codex Ephraemi (C), as Swete's notes give it
readings.en: finding of wisdom
readings.plain: finding wisdom

readings.w: Hebrew manuscript B of the Cairo Genizah (folio X recto, line 12), אהבת דודים
readings.en: love of beloved ones
readings.plain: the love of friends

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Greek. The Hebrew of manuscript B reads "love of dodim," a word that can mean friends or lovers, as in the Song of Songs (Song of Songs 5:1).

a: advice held in high regard
p: The Plain English Translation follows the correctors of Vaticanus and the other codices, with the Latin: "counsel." The first hand of Vaticanus, which Swete prints, has "a wife."

readings.w: Greek: the correctors of Codex Vaticanus (B), Codex Sinaiticus (ℵ), Codex Alexandrinus (A) and Codex Ephraemi (C), βουλή, as Swete's notes give them; the Latin Vulgate (its 40:25), "consilium beneplacitum"; the KJV ("counsel"); Hebrew: Kahana's edition of manuscript B of the Cairo Genizah, עצה טובה, "good counsel" (Kahana's reading only: the leaf is now lost at this word, and Abegg's transcription of folio X recto, line 17, keeps only the start of the line, זהב וכס]ף)
readings.en: above both counsel is esteemed
readings.plain: advice held in high regard

readings.w: Greek: the first hand of Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as Swete prints it
readings.en: above both a wife is esteemed
readings.plain: a wife held in high regard

why: The Plain English Translation departs from Swete's printed text here, as it does at 43:8, 43:9, 43:23 and 43:26. Every other Greek witness in Swete's notes, including the correctors of Vaticanus itself, has "counsel," and so does the Latin; the only Hebrew is Kahana's, and it agrees. "A wife" looks like a slip from 40:19 and 40:23, where a wife is the better thing.

a: and they have covered him with more than any glory
p: The Greek is strange; the Hebrew says the fear of God has its canopy over all glory, the words of Isaiah 4:5.

readings.w: Greek: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD) as printed by Swete and the other Greek copies
readings.orig: καὶ ὑπὲρ πᾶσαν δόξαν ἐκάλυψαν αὐτόν
readings.en: and above all glory they covered him
readings.plain: and they have covered him with more than any glory

readings.w: Hebrew: the Masada scroll (first century BC), damaged, and Kahana's edition of manuscript B of the Cairo Genizah (the leaf now reads וכן, "and so," for ועל)
readings.en: and over all glory is its canopy
readings.plain: and its canopy is spread over all glory

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Greek, which may be a loose rendering. The Hebrew uses Isaiah's picture of a canopy (chuppah) over the glory on Mount Zion: "for a canopy will cover all the glory" (Isaiah 4:5).

a: who resists everyone and can bear no more
p: The Greek says "disobedient," like the main text of manuscript B; the Masada scroll and the margin of B speak of sight that is gone.

readings.w: Greek: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD) as printed by Swete; Hebrew: the main text of manuscript B of the Cairo Genizah (folio X verso, line 10), סרב ואבד תקוה, "contrary, and has lost hope"
readings.en: disobedient and having lost patience
readings.plain: who resists everyone and can bear no more

readings.w: Hebrew: the Masada scroll (first century BC), column III, line 2, אפס המרה ואבוד תקוה, which Eric Reymond translates "one lacking vision, void of hope." It spells המרה without the alef of the margin's המראה
readings.en: lacking sight, void of hope
readings.plain: whose sight is gone and who has lost hope

readings.w: Hebrew: two notes in the margin of manuscript B (folio X verso, line 10), אפס המראה ואבד תקוה
readings.en: whose sight is gone and who has lost hope
readings.plain: whose sight is gone and who has lost hope

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Greek, which agrees in sense with the main text of manuscript B, סרב, "contrary." The margin of B has "sight is gone" (המראה). The Masada scroll writes המרה, without the alef; Reymond's translation takes it as "vision," the margin's meaning.

a: Human mourning is for the body
p: The Greek has "mourning"; the Hebrew has hevel, "vapor." Goes with the next entry.

readings.w: Greek: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD) as printed by Swete and the other Greek copies
readings.en: the mourning of humans is in their bodies
readings.plain: Human mourning is for the body

readings.w: Hebrew manuscript B of the Cairo Genizah, הבל אדם בגויתו; the Masada scroll is damaged but keeps the first letters
readings.en: a human's vapor is in his body
readings.plain: A human being is a vapor in his body

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Greek. The Hebrew uses hevel, the "vapor" of Ecclesiastes 1:2: the body passes away like a breath. This entry and the next one go together.

a: but the name of sinners, which is not good, will be wiped out
t: A sinner's name, or a name of loyal love?
p: The Greek wipes out sinners' names; the Hebrew says a name of loyal love lasts. Goes with the entry before.

readings.w: Greek: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD) as printed by Swete
readings.orig: ὄνομα δὲ ἁμαρτωλῶν οὐκ ἀγαθὸν ἐξαλειφθήσεται
readings.en: but the name of sinners, not good, will be wiped out
readings.plain: but the name of sinners, which is not good, will be wiped out

readings.w: Hebrew: the Masada scroll (first century BC), שם חסד ללא יכרת, and manuscript B of the Cairo Genizah, אך שם חסד לא יכרת
readings.en: but a name of loyal love will not be cut off
readings.plain: but a name of loyal love will never be cut off

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Greek. The Hebrew, which both Hebrew copies support, sets the passing body against a lasting good name, the theme of 41:12-13. This entry and the one before go together.

a: before the truth of God and the covenant
p: The Greek has "the truth of God and covenant"; the Hebrew has "breaking an oath and a covenant."

readings.w: Greek: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD) as printed by Swete
readings.orig: καὶ ἀπὸ ἀληθείας θεοῦ καὶ διαθήκης
readings.en: and from the truth of God and covenant
readings.plain: before the truth of God and the covenant

readings.w: Hebrew: the Masada scroll (first century BC), מהפר אלה וברית; manuscript B of the Cairo Genizah is damaged at the start but has אלה וברית
readings.en: of breaking an oath and a covenant
readings.plain: of breaking an oath and a covenant

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Greek. The Hebrew makes the shameful act clear: going back on a sworn agreement.

a: eyeing a courtesan
p: Vaticanus has hetaira, "courtesan"; Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus, Ephraemi and the Masada scroll have "another" or "a strange" woman.

readings.w: Greek: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD) as printed by Swete; the Latin Vulgate (its 41:25), "mulieris fornicariae"; the KJV ("an harlot")
readings.en: looking at a courtesan
readings.plain: eyeing a courtesan

readings.w: Greek: Codex Sinaiticus (ℵ), Codex Alexandrinus (A) and Codex Ephraemi (C), ἑτέρας, as Swete's notes give them; Hebrew: the Masada scroll (first century BC), column IV, line 1, ומהתבונן אל זרה, which Eric Reymond translates "and of noticing a foreign woman" (manuscript B is damaged here)
readings.en: looking at another woman
readings.plain: eyeing another woman

why: The Plain English Translation follows the base text. The two Greek words differ by one letter. The other codices and the Masada scroll agree on "another" or "strange" woman, the "strange woman" of Proverbs (Proverbs 5:20).

a: the very old man who quarrels with young men
t: A quarrelsome old man, or a lecherous one?
p: The Greek has an old man disputing with the young; the Hebrew has an old man busy with sexual sin.

readings.w: Greek: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD) as printed by Swete
readings.en: a very old man disputing with young men
readings.plain: the very old man who quarrels with young men

readings.w: Hebrew: the Masada scroll (first century BC), ב כושל ענה בזנות, and the margin of manuscript B of the Cairo Genizah, ושב כושל ועונה בזנות
readings.en: an old man who stumbles, busied with fornication
readings.plain: the old man who stumbles into sexual sin

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Greek. Both Hebrew copies speak of an old man and sexual sin; the main text of manuscript B has a longer form of the same idea.

a: a woman who brings shame brings disgrace
t: A woman, a house, or a daughter?
p: The second line differs in every copy. The Masada scroll and the margin of manuscript B speak of a daughter.

readings.w: Greek: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD) as printed by Swete, with no difference in Swete's notes; the Latin Vulgate
readings.en: and a woman who shames, to reproach
readings.plain: a woman who brings shame brings disgrace

readings.w: Hebrew: the margin of manuscript B of the Cairo Genizah (folio XII recto, line 4), ובת מחרפת תביע חרפה
readings.en: and a daughter who shames pours out disgrace
readings.plain: a daughter who brings shame brings disgrace

readings.w: Hebrew: the Masada scroll (first century BC), column IV, line 25, ובת מפחדת מבול חרפה, which Eric Reymond translates "(better even) than the daughter who dreads every (read מכול) reproach"
readings.en: than a daughter who dreads every reproach
readings.plain: better even than a daughter who fears every disgrace

readings.w: Hebrew: the main text of manuscript B (folio XII recto, line 4), ובית מחרפת תביע אשה, which Abegg and Parker translate "And a woman pours out a houseful of reproach"
readings.en: and a woman pours out a houseful of reproach
readings.plain: a woman pours out a houseful of disgrace

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Greek. The first line is the same in the Greek, manuscript B and the Masada scroll. In the second line the Masada scroll, copied in the first century BC, and the margin of B have "daughter," which ties the saying to the father's worry over his daughter in 42:9-11.

a: I have pondered
p: Vaticanus has a first person verb; Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and the Hebrew have God as the one who understands.

readings.w: Greek: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD) as printed by Swete
readings.en: and in their cunning I pondered
readings.plain: I have pondered

readings.w: Greek: Codex Sinaiticus (ℵ) and Codex Alexandrinus (A), διενοήθη; Hebrew: the Masada scroll (first century BC) and manuscript B of the Cairo Genizah, ובמערמיהם יתבונן
readings.en: and he understood their cunning
readings.plain: he has understood

why: The Plain English Translation follows Vaticanus, which suddenly lets the poet speak. The other reading, one letter shorter in Greek, keeps God as the subject throughout, as the Hebrew does, and may be original.

a: the Lord knows
t: The Lord, or the Most High?
p: Vaticanus has "the Lord"; Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and the Masada scroll have "the Most High."

readings.w: Greek: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD) as printed by Swete
readings.en: for the Lord knew
readings.plain: the Lord knows

readings.w: Greek: Codex Sinaiticus (ℵ), Codex Alexandrinus (A) and probably the first hand of Codex Ephraemi (C); Hebrew: the Masada scroll (first century BC), כי ידע עליון
readings.en: for the Most High knew
readings.plain: the Most High knows

why: The Plain English Translation follows the base text. The difference does not change the meaning; it is entered because the Masada scroll agrees with the other Greek codices.

a: It is an instrument for the camps on high
p: The Plain English Translation departs from Vaticanus's "parables" to follow the other codices and the Hebrew: "camps."

readings.w: Greek: Codex Sinaiticus (ℵ), Codex Alexandrinus (A) and Codex Ephraemi (C), παρεμβολῶν; Hebrew: the Masada scroll (first century BC) and manuscript B of the Cairo Genizah, כלי צבא, "an instrument of the army"
readings.en: an instrument of the camps on high
readings.plain: It is an instrument for the camps on high

readings.w: Greek: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD) as printed by Swete
readings.en: an instrument of parables on high
readings.plain: It is an instrument of likenesses on high

why: The Plain English Translation departs from the base text here. Vaticanus's paraboloon differs from paremboloon by two letters and gives no clear sense; the Hebrew "army" (tsava') agrees with "camps," the stars as God's army. The Plain English Translation renders skeuos "instrument" here, as at 43:2.

a: in the Lord's high places
p: Here the Plain English Translation departs from Vaticanus's "the Lord" (as subject) and follows "of the Lord" with the other codices.

readings.w: Greek: a corrector of Codex Sinaiticus (ℵ c.a), Codex Alexandrinus (A) and Codex Ephraemi (C), Κυρίου; manuscript B of the Cairo Genizah has במרומי אל, "in the heights of God"
readings.en: in the highest places of the Lord
readings.plain: in the Lord's high places

readings.w: Greek: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD) as printed by Swete
readings.en: in the highest places, the Lord
readings.plain: in the high places: the Lord

why: The Plain English Translation departs from the base text. In Vaticanus the last word is in the form of a subject, which leaves the line without sense; the other codices and the Hebrew read "of the Lord" or "of God."

a: by holy words
t: Holy words, or the Holy One's words?
p: Vaticanus has "holy words"; the other codices have "the words of the Holy One"; the Hebrew has "the word of the Lord."

readings.w: Greek: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD) as printed by Swete
readings.en: by holy words
readings.plain: by holy words

readings.w: Greek: Codex Sinaiticus (ℵ), Codex Alexandrinus (A) and Codex Ephraemi (C), ἁγίου, as Swete's notes give them; the KJV ("At the commandment of the Holy One")
readings.en: by the words of the Holy One
readings.plain: by the Holy One's words

readings.w: Hebrew: the Masada scroll (first century BC), column VI, line 3, בדבר אדני; manuscript B of the Cairo Genizah (folio XII verso, line 12), בדבר אל
readings.en: by the word of the Lord
readings.plain: by the Lord's word

why: The Plain English Translation follows the base text. The other codices and the Hebrew agree that the word is God's; in Vaticanus "holy" describes the words themselves.

a: makes the snow settle
t: Settles the snow, or hurries it?
p: Swete prints "settled" (katepausen); a corrector of Vaticanus, Alexandrinus and Ephraemi have "hurried" (katespeusen).

readings.plain: makes the snow settle

readings.plain: makes the snow hurry

why: The Plain English Translation follows the base text. The two verbs differ by one letter. The Hebrew copies do not have snow here at all (see the note on this verse).

a: His thunder's roar reproaches the earth
t: Reproaches, or makes the earth writhe?
p: Most Greek copies have "reproached"; Alexandrinus and the Hebrew have "made the earth writhe."

readings.w: Greek: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD) as printed by Swete; Codex Sinaiticus (ℵ)
readings.en: the voice of his thunder reproached the earth
readings.plain: His thunder's roar reproaches the earth

readings.w: Greek: Codex Alexandrinus (A), ὠδίνησεν; Hebrew: the Masada scroll (first century BC) and manuscript B of the Cairo Genizah, קול רעמו יחיל ארצו
readings.en: the voice of his thunder made the earth writhe
readings.plain: His thunder's roar makes the earth writhe

why: The Plain English Translation follows the base text. Alexandrinus agrees with the Hebrew "makes his earth writhe" (as in Psalm 29:8, where the LORD's voice makes the wilderness writhe), which may be the original Greek.

a: and in it he planted islands
p: Here the Plain English Translation departs from Swete's text, "Jesus (Joshua) planted it," and follows the Hebrew and Latin, "islands."

readings.w: Hebrew manuscript B of the Cairo Genizah, ויט בתהום איים, "and he spread out islands in the deep"; the Masada scroll (first century BC) keeps the last word, איים; the Latin Vulgate, plantavit in illa Dominus insulas, "the Lord planted islands in it"; the KJV ("planteth islands therein")
readings.en: islands
readings.plain: and in it he planted islands

readings.w: Greek: Codex Vaticanus (B) and Codex Sinaiticus (ℵ) write ΙΣ, the short form of the name, which Swete prints as Ἰησοῦς; Codex Alexandrinus (A) and Codex Ephraemi (C) write Ἰησοῦς in full
readings.en: and Jesus (Joshua) planted it
readings.plain: and Jesus planted it

why: The Plain English Translation departs from the base text. The Hebrew has "islands" in both copies that keep the line. In Greek capitals, ΝΗΣΟΥΣ ("islands") and ΙΗΣΟΥΣ ("Jesus") differ by one letter, and the short form ΙΣ in Vaticanus and Sinaiticus shows that a scribe took the word for the name. The Latin "the Lord planted islands" seems to keep both.
b: The Greek name Iēsous is the form of Joshua used in the Septuagint, and it is Ben Sira's own name (50:27). The reading is old and spread through the great codices, but a scribal error is the simplest explanation. No reader needs to see a prophecy of Christ here, and the Latin, the Catholic Church's traditional text, has "islands."

a: and the race of sea monsters
p: Vaticanus has "sea monsters"; Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus have "cattle"; the Masada scroll has Rahab, the sea dragon.

readings.w: Hebrew: the Masada scroll (first century BC), גבורת רהב; manuscript B of the Cairo Genizah has וגבורות רבה, "and mighty things of the deep"

readings.plain: and the might of Rahab

why: The Plain English Translation follows Vaticanus, which fits the sea. "Cattle" is a slip of a few letters. The Masada reading names Rahab, the sea monster that God defeated (Job 26:12; Isaiah 51:9), here simply one of his creatures; Ben Sira tames the old myth.

a: each thing comes safely to its end
t: A good journey, a sweet smell, or a messenger?
p: The Plain English Translation follows Sinaiticus's "success" over Vaticanus's "fragrance." The Hebrew speaks of a messenger.
